title: Doing it wrong
author: arkaine_23
selftext:
Amateur hour.  I lack knowledge in all relevant areas but I'm still working toward a degree of trading automation.  So given my limits here's the concept I'm working on.  I'm pretty sure that if I get this working, it will self destruct my account in short order.  Anyway....  I have skills with things like powershell and bash, and wouldn't have trouble setting up.virtual hosts or running my own servers.   When coding outside what I know, I partner with AI's to muddle through​.  I don't know python.  I have no significant trading skills either, just vibes.



The outlune of my bot is:



An AI signal app's alerts > 



AHK script on a PC > 



injest some internet data > 



evaluate conditions for go/no-go/risk level >



activate a webull hotkey to buy & TP/SL.  



If I'm around and monitoring, I'll manage adjustments after that initial order.  If not, pray the strategy is sound.  The goal is to quickly get aboard intraday big movers and exit with a conservative amount of profit or cut losses and bail on them if they fail or I'm late entering.

  
1)  Function for getting alerts   

I'll use someone else's signal/scanner AI.  I've been playing with an app called Pro Ticker Signals.   It sends iOS/Android notifications (subject to some delay), or if you have the app open you can​ refresh it's scan page for potentially faster access to its real time alerts.   These seem to mostly come premarket or around market open.   I've only been watching it for a short time, but it's been finding a handful of big intraday movers every day.   

The trick is moving fast enough. I'm mostly late in arriving because I'm asleep or working when those alerts come in and I wind up just gambling on the volatility after they've peaked and try to make a few of bucks/day from my tiny for-fun webull account.  I want to get entry automatically and build in a conservative bit of profiting on a rise and exiting on a fall as a baseline play, and see how it does.  Then I can figure out other things to try to safeguard it and optimizie it further.   



I'll need to keep an app open and refreshing and then from what it displays read text.and parse it for the data I want.  I'll use regular expressions to collect ticker names and entry/Long prices from the signal texts (ignoring short signals for now).  



2)  Function to collect other info about a ticker.

I'll also scrape yahoo http to get an alerted ticker's current (or at least its ballpark price).   I want to ignore tickers that have a current price or signaled entry price less than $1, and also ignore them if the current price is already more than 20% higher than the signal's entry price.   If the price is below the signal's.entry, then I'll loop a price re-check until current price is greater than or equal to entry price.   This loop would have a sleep period of let's say 3s per price re-evaluation, and a max limit of 300 cycles before deciding to ignore the ticker.  

  
3)  if price loop conditions were met, bring webull desktop into focus and execute one of several preset buy order hotkeys.   I'll wrap some logic around choosing which buy preset and exiting strategy to use.  I may try to read my account's settled cash so I can dynamically use a small % of that per trade, or just hardcode a max $ value per buy in the script.

  
Set a max of X tickers to execute buy orders for per day. 



At midnight, reset:  clear ingored and activated tickers and the buy count daily.  Injest or request a new available per-trade $ limit for the next day.  Cycle to a new log file, clean up any temp data/files.
